Rachel,

We experienced a severe regression in production this morning between 06:40–07:25 PDT. Our customer-facing API saw a ~40% drop in throughput and a sustained 5xx rate averaging 6.2% for that window (incident IDs GE-20260720-01 / GE-20260720-02). P99 latency spiked from our baseline of 120ms to ~1.1s for several critical routes. This impacted our checkout and search flows, and we had to failover to a cached path which cost us revenue and manual ops work.

We need an explanation, the corrective plan, and clarification on how this maps to the SLA credit mechanics in our contract (section 5.2). Please escalate to your ops and sales leadership — this is impacting our execs, and we may need a formal remediation and credit arrangement.

Can we get a proposed remediation timeline and a preliminary credit estimate by EOD PT?

Thanks,

Folks — forwarding Samantha's escalation. Need guidance on: credit calc (contract section 5.2), approval authority for >$50k credits, and whether Legal needs to pre-approve an amendment template.

Proposed quick math (preliminary):
- Affected window: 45 minutes (06:40–07:25 PDT)
- Measured SLA breach: error rate above 5% threshold + p99 latency > SLA for two routes (checkout, search)
- Contract baseline: monthly uptime/availability and error rate credit tiers; no explicit revenue-linked reimbursements.

Option A (conservative): Supply pro-rated service credits per SLA table (month % x committed minimum monthly fee).
Option B (commercial): Offer one-time commercial credit tied to customer-reported impact + 2 weeks of Dedicated burst capacity at no charge (operational goodwill).

I'm inclined to Option B for preservation of the relationship; we can cap at $75k and include a contractual amendment that clarifies the credit formula for multi-route incidents. Marcus — do we have authority to sign off on that level or should we loop in Marissa/VP Sales? Laura — Legal input?

—Rachel

Samantha / Tim / Elaine —

Thanks again for the patience while we triaged last week's outage. Per our conversation, attached is a formal proposal outlining remediation steps, the proposed credit, and a draft contract amendment for clarity going forward. Highlights below:

Summary of findings (interim):
- Root cause (infra): autoscaling policy applied conservative backoff during a warm model weights refresh which, combined with elevated retry rates, caused transient capacity starvation across a subset of your routed instances. Full RCA to follow.

Proposed remediation package:
1) Financial — One-time commercial credit of $62,500 applied to your next invoice (represents roughly 25% of the committed monthly minimum for July; conscious cap to balance precedent).
2) Operational — Two weeks of Dedicated burst capacity (equivalent to 8 GPU-days) to be available through Aug 10, 2026 at no charge.
3) Contractual — Amendment draft clarifying multi-route aggregated incidents and a streamlined calculation for multi-route credits (attached). This will be a short addendum to section 5.2.

Next steps we request from GlobalEdge:
- Confirm acceptance by EOD Fri 2026-07-30 or provide requested edits to the amendment.
- If accepted, we will: (a) generate a DocuSign for the amendment, (b) apply the credit to your Aug invoice, and (c) schedule an architectural review with our infra team to prevent recurrence.

Attachments: GlobalEdge_SLA_Credit_Proposal_20260727.xlsx (credit table), amendment_draft_GlobalEdge_v1.docx

If the proposed commercial credit does not meet your expectations, we're open to discuss a narrow increase but would ask for a final decision quickly to avoid billing cycles slipping.
